rubrics.reason: All exact topics, counterevidence and distinct challenge completed in this run.

assessment.rationale: Four-year reported group cash realization is 104.21%, but FY2025 falls to 90.24%; positive post-acquisition cash is not owner FCFE. Targeted original-page review now identifies actual WC/tax/interest cash adjustments, deferred revenue and completion-based service recognition. This resolves the bounded recognition/WC challenge sufficiently for a qualified research band, without declaring exhaustive one-off or contract-compliance review.

evidence.rationale: Reported group cash is realized over four full-year windows; no group cash is assigned to parent/NCI by profit ratio and acquisition spending is not maintenance.

The original income page separates 91.956869021 billion VND other profit from 13.043632833797 trillion pretax profit and 2.977156356773 trillion finance income. Finance income is not presumed recurring or automatically removed. Full one-off coverage remains unproven and prevents a strong/max band.

The original cash statement identifies receivable, inventory, payable and prepaid cash adjustments, actual tax/interest paid and other operating payments. This bypasses using an unqualified restated closing-balance ratio; the Note39 classification bridge remains a separate vintage, not a TTM/scope bridge.

Reviewed policies distinguish unperformed advance receipts from earnings, completion-estimate software services, time-based telecom and semester tuition. These identify concrete timing/estimation risks, not assurance every contract complied.

counterevidence.rationale: FY2025 cash lags group profit and cash acquisition spending rises; receivable and prepaid cash use are real counterevidence against an unqualified strong-realization judgment.

Recognition depends partly on completion estimates, finance-income recurrence is not exhaustively proved, and no full-year FTEL cash/scope bridge is established. These qualifications remain after a limited page review.

disconfirmingEvidence: FY2025 cash lags group profit and cash acquisition spending rises; receivable and prepaid cash use are real counterevidence against an unqualified strong-realization judgment.

Recognition depends partly on completion estimates, finance-income recurrence is not exhaustively proved, and no full-year FTEL cash/scope bridge is established. These qualifications remain after a limited page review.
assumptions: AS_REVISED FY2025 original consolidated reporting; FY22–FY25 reported cash ratios are diagnostics, not the M3 normalized ratio.
No maintenance capex, recurring finance-income estimate or common cash allocation is invented.
invalidationConditions: Revised source columns or cash statements break same-scope realization.
Material unrecognized losses, recurring receivable noncollection, or contract-estimate corrections undermine the qualified cash reading.

counterTests: Reject a 5–6 strong band based only on cumulative cash conversion.
Check cash adjustments against original page13; do not use restated closing receivables as cash flow.
Policy disclosure is not transaction-level recognition assurance; exhaustive one-off and common-cash review remain incomplete.
No parent/NCI allocation, maintenance-capex inference or fund double deduction.
challengeDisposition.rationale: Accept bounded cash realization/adjustment quality, but lower preparation 4/6 to 3/6. Actual WC/tax/interest cash bridges and explicit recognition policies close the selected challenge; finance recurrence, contract estimates, lower FY2025 conversion and incomplete exhaustive one-offs remain material qualifications. This is not a claim of clean normalized earnings.
